newsitem.title: UK: T-bonds steady in London, PPI seen supportive.
newsitem.headline: T-bonds steady in London, PPI seen supportive.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries were little changed in London trade on Friday, but dealers said benign producer price data later may provide a bit of a tonic.
Any rally would likely be muted however, with investors reluctant to take long positions ahead of key activity data next week, in particular retail sales.

"I think the market will rally, but we've rallied a lot already this week and 6.50 percent on the long bond could prove a sticky level in the market," said Adam Chester, international bond strategist at Yamaichi International Europe.
"People will be wary of going long, ahead of what is a very important set of activity numbers next week."

Chester said June retail sales data, consumer prices and industrial production data due next week would dictate whether the Treasury market can climb higher, or whether it is in for a more significant correction.
"The retail sales data in particular are important. The consumer sector is the key focus -- if consumer spending starts picking up, the market will be in for a bit of a sell-off," said Chester.
By 1030 GMT, the 30-year long bond was at 100-26 to yield 6.56 percent, unchanged from Tokyo and up from 100-25 at the New York close.
The 10-year note was at 102-23, unchanged from Tokyo and up from 102-22 in New York.
Charles Quigley, U.S. bond salesman at Chase in London, said the general consensus that inflation was not an issue for the time being had left the Treasury market scrabbling for inspiration.
He said short term, the market was looking slightly toppy, leaving it vulnerable to a bit of a setback.
"The correction seems overdue from a sentiment standpoint," he said.
He said the Treasury market may be suffering from a touch of corporate bond-induced indigestion, given the volume of issuance recently.
Analysts and dealers said the market was not unduly worried about the producer price data due at 1230 GMT.
According to a Reuter poll, economists expect the PPI to be unchanged month on month in June after falling 0.3 percent in May.
"The PPI has largely been discounted at being relatively weak...which should provide a supportive backdrop to the market," said Chester.
